question: Let $f(x),g(x)$ be functions on the real line $\mathbb R$ such that both $f(x)+g(x)$ and $f(x)g(x)$ are differentiable. Which of the following is FALSE?

options.B: $f(x)$ is differentiable if and only if $g(x)$ is differentiable.
options.D: If $f(x)>g(x)$ for all $x\in\mathbb R$, then $f(x)$ is differentiable.
